interactions.title: Pay them a compliment
interactions.note: Free. Costs you nothing but the sentence.

good: "You noticed the hair. Two days late, but you noticed."
"Say that again on a day you're not asking me for anything."
"That was nice. Don't ruin it by explaining why you said it."
"Alright. I'll take it. I'll be insufferable about it too."
bad: "You said the same thing at the wedding. Word for word."
"That's your investor voice. I know your investor voice."
"Thanks. Are you about to tell me you're working the weekend?"
"Mm." That's it. That's the whole reply.

good: They went bright red and pretended to look for something.
"I KNOW." Then they told you about it for eleven minutes.
They wrote it down. You saw them write it down.
"You're not just saying that?" You were not just saying that.
bad: "You didn't even look at it properly." Correct.
"Is this because you missed Thursday?" Also correct.
They shrugged with their whole body. Impressive, technically.
"Okay." Door. Music, slightly too loud.

good: "Careful, that almost sounded sincere."
"Screenshotting this. It goes in the speech."
"Right back at you, mate. Now buy me a coffee."
"I needed that today, actually. Don't make it weird."
bad: "You're being nice. What have you done."
"Is this the bit before you ask me for something?"
"Mate, you're eight months late on that one."
"Thanks?" You could hear the question mark.

good: They said thanks twice and then had a very good afternoon.
"That's the first time anyone's said that out loud here."
They told three people. One of them told you they'd heard.
"Cheers. I'll put that in my review, if we ever do reviews."
bad: "You've got the wrong ticket. That was Priya's."
"Is this the bit before the reorg?" Fair, honestly.
They said thanks in the flat voice people use for HR.
"Great. Could I have the headcount instead?"

good: "Kind of you to remember. Most people don't."
"You're smoother than you were at the last thing."
"Flattery works on me. It's my only real weakness."
"That's the nicest thing anyone's said to me in this industry."
bad: "You've got me confused with the other one at the fund."
"Mm. What is it you actually want?"
"That's what you said last time. I keep notes."
They smiled the way people smile at a pitch they won't take.

interactions.title: Apologise
interactions.note: Worth most where you've done the most damage.

good: "Thank you. That's all I wanted. That's genuinely all it was."
"Okay. Okay. Come here."
"You didn't say 'but'. I noticed you didn't say 'but'."
"We're fine. Eat something, you look like a founder."
bad: "You're apologising for the symptom again."
"That's the third one this quarter. I've stopped counting them separately."
"Don't apologise. Change the calendar."
"Fine." It was not fine.

good: "It's okay." It wasn't, but they meant it.
They hugged you sideways, which is the maximum available.
"You can come to the next one instead." Deal.
"Adults don't usually say sorry properly. That was properly."
bad: "You said that about the sports day too."
"It's fine, it's fine, it's fine." Three fines is not fine.
They said "okay" and went back to the game.
"Can you just not promise next time?"

good: "Consider it forgotten. Mostly. Ninety percent forgotten."
"We're good. You owe me a curry, but we're good."
"Thanks for saying it. Most people just go quiet for a year."
"Ah, stop. Come round Sunday."
bad: "You didn't have to. That's sort of the problem."
"Right." Long pause. "Right."
"It's been fourteen months, mate."
"I'd rather you just called more."

good: "Appreciated. Genuinely. Nobody up there does that."
"Okay. Clean slate. Where do you want me Monday?"
They looked surprised, then relieved, then busy again.
"That took something to say. Thanks."
bad: "Sorry doesn't unship it, though, does it."
"Is this an apology or a retention conversation?"
"Noted." They wrote it down. That's worse.
"I'd have preferred the four days back."

good: "Water under it. This industry is six people, anyway."
"Decent of you. Most founders just wait it out."
"Forgotten. Send me the deck again, properly this time."
"Fine. Coffee. You're paying and you're on time."
bad: "You emailed. That's not the same as calling."
"Mm. I've heard the sentence before."
"It's not personal. It just isn't a yes."
They accepted it politely and did not warm up at all.

good: They took the call. Fifteen minutes, no lawyers. Something cooled.
"We'd both look better if this stopped." Agreed, apparently.
A short joint statement. Nobody meant a word and it worked.
"You went first. I'll remember that." Said almost warmly.
bad: "Apology accepted," they said, in a way that meant the opposite.
They forwarded your message to a journalist. Nice.
No reply. The silence was doing the talking.
"We're not enemies," they said. "You're just smaller."

good: "You are so bad at this and it works every single time."
"Put the laptop down and say that again."
"Absolutely not. Ask me again at nine."
They laughed properly. The one from before the company.
bad: "You've got a spreadsheet open behind me. I can see it."
"Is this instead of the conversation we said we'd have?"
"Not tonight. Not because of you. Mostly not because of you."
"You smell like the office." Reader, you did.

good: "You're trouble," they said, and did not move away.
They laughed and asked what you were doing Thursday.
"Careful. I'm terrible at boundaries and worse at gossip."
The conversation stopped being about the deck an hour ago.
bad: "I'm going to pretend that was about the cap table."
They looked at your ring finger, then at their drink.
"Let's keep this professional. It's a small industry."
"You've got a partner. I've got a memory."

interactions.title: Tell them something true
interactions.note: The real number, the real fear. Expensive if it lands wrong.

good: "Thank you for not doing the brave voice."
"I already knew. I was waiting for you to say it."
"Right. Then we work out the plan together. Sit down."
They held your hand and asked exactly one good question.
bad: "How long have you been sitting on that?" Too long.
"And you told the investors first. Of course you did."
"I can't be the only person you talk to about this."
They went very quiet and started tidying things.

good: "Mate. Right. Pub. Now. Bring the numbers."
"Everyone's faking it. You're just faking it in public."
"Thanks for telling me and not the internet."
They didn't offer advice. They just stayed on the phone.
bad: "I don't really know what to say to that, if I'm honest."
"Have you spoken to someone? A proper someone?"
The conversation got very practical, very fast.
"Yeah, work's mad for me too." It was not the same.

good: "I'd rather know. Everyone would rather know."
"Okay. What do you need from me to fix it?"
They squared their shoulders and cleared their afternoon.
"Thanks for treating me like an adult."
bad: You watched them decide to update their CV tonight.
"That's... a lot to put on the person who ships the build."
It was around the office by four. Not maliciously. Just fast.
"Should I be worried?" Yes. "Right."

good: "Everyone's book looks like that. Nobody says it."
"Useful. I'll stop pretending too. Here's mine."
"You've just made me more likely to back you, oddly."
"That's the most honest twenty minutes I've had all month."
bad: "I'm going to forget you told me that. Try to."
It surfaced in someone else's diligence call. Fast industry.
"Right. Well. Let's revisit next quarter." Never.
They were kind about it, which was somehow worse.

interactions.title: Brag about them to someone else
interactions.note: It always gets back to them. That's the mechanism.

good: It got back to them. They pretended not to care for a week.
"You told your investors about my thing?" Yes. "Weird. Good weird."
They put it in their bio. Their actual bio.
"Did you actually say that or is this a dad thing?" You said it.
bad: "Please stop telling strangers about me."
You got a detail wrong. They will mention it for years.
"That was two years ago. I do other things now."
"Cool." They left the room to have a feeling privately.

good: "Someone at a conference quoted you about me. Bizarre. Lovely."
"You're my agent now, apparently."
It got them a call. The call went somewhere.
"I heard what you said. Thank you. Shut up."
bad: "Bit much, mate."
You oversold it and now someone's asking them for something.
"Please don't do my networking for me."
"You made me sound like a LinkedIn post."

good: It got back to them within a day. They walked taller for a week.
"You said that to an investor? About me?"
A recruiter called them. They said no, and told you they'd said no.
"Right, well, now I have to actually be that good."
bad: You named the wrong project. Everyone heard which one.
"Nice. Could that go in the salary band instead?"
A recruiter called them. They took the call.
"Don't do that in front of the team. It makes it worse for me."

good: "Somebody said you'd been talking me up. Unexpectedly decent of you."
It reached them by Thursday. They opened your last email.
"You've got a reputation for slagging people off. Not this week."
"That's a favour. I'll remember it's a favour."
bad: "You made it sound like we're closer than we are."
You attributed someone else's deal to them. Awkward.
"Please don't use my name in rooms I'm not in."
It read as name-dropping, because it was.

interactions.title: Buy them something
interactions.note: The team's gift is on the Team tab. This one's personal.

good: "You remembered the specific one. The specific one!"
"This is very expensive and I love it and we're discussing money later."
They wore it out that evening, which was the whole point.
"You didn't have to." They did not put it down all night.
bad: "You bought me a thing instead of a Tuesday."
"It's lovely. Can we talk about the calendar now?"
Wrong size. Wrong colour. Right idea, wrong everything.
"Did the office order this?" The office ordered this.

good: Ninety seconds of unfiltered joy. Worth every penny.
"HOW did you know?" You listened once, in March.
They took it to school. It came back famous.
They said thank you without being asked. Note the date.
bad: "I said that a year ago." They did.
"Is this a sorry present?" It was a sorry present.
They liked the box more than the thing. Fair.
"Cool, thanks." Straight to the shelf. Still there.

good: "You absolute idiot. I love it. Come here."
"This is the least practical thing I own. It's going on the wall."
"You've been listening. That's the alarming part."
They sent a photo of it in position. Twice.
bad: "Mate, this is too much. It's genuinely too much."
"Now I have to get you something and I have no money."
"Is this because you cancelled twice?" Yes. "Right."
It sat in the hall unopened for three weeks.

good: "Well, that's not a mug with your logo on it. Thank you."
"I'll declare this and keep it. In that order."
"Very smooth. You'll do well in this industry."
They replied within the hour for the first time all year.
bad: "I can't accept this. Our compliance people are odd about it."
"That's a lot of money to spend on a maybe."
"This feels like it comes with an invoice."
It got sent back with a very polite note.

interactions.title: Take them out for the evening
interactions.note: The dear one: an evening and a bill, and it almost always works.

good: No phones on the table. Three hours. You both noticed.
"That was the version of you I married."
You talked about something that wasn't runway. Revolutionary.
"Same time next week?" You said yes and meant it.
bad: You took one call. One. It was a long call.
"Nice place." Two hours of nice place and not much else.
You fell asleep in the taxi. They paid the taxi.
Lovely dinner, spent mostly rehearsing Monday's board deck.

good: They ordered the most expensive thing. You let them. Correct.
Two hours of a subject you know nothing about. Excellent.
"This was actually good." High praise. Bank it.
They asked about the company. Properly asked. You told them.
bad: They were on their phone. So were you. Symmetry.
You picked the restaurant you like. They noticed.
"Can we go home now?" Forty minutes in.
It was fine. Fine is not the word you were going for.

good: Closed the place. Solved two of their problems and none of yours.
"First proper night out I've had since the baby. Thank you."
You laughed until it hurt about something from 2011.
"Same again next month. Put it in the diary now."
bad: You talked about the company for two hours and heard yourself doing it.
They got the earlier train. You noticed which train it was.
Nice evening. Slightly like a meeting.
"You alright? You seem somewhere else." You were.

good: "Best pitch I've had all year and you didn't pitch me once."
They introduced you to somebody on the way out.
"Right. Send me the thing. I'll actually read it."
Four hours. Two bottles. One warm intro on Monday.
bad: "I'll expense my half, if that's alright." It was a signal.
They took a call at the table and did not come back quickly.
You pitched at the starter. It never recovered.
Perfectly pleasant. Absolutely nothing moved.

interactions.title: Insult them
interactions.note: It never costs nothing. The roll only decides how much.

good: "That was beneath you." It was. They let it go anyway.
They went to bed early without saying goodnight.
"I'm going to assume that was the week talking."
The room got cold and stayed cold for an hour.
bad: "Say that again and mean it, or take it back properly."
They repeated it back to you slowly. It sounded much worse.
"You talk to your investors better than you talk to me."
The door didn't slam. Somehow that was worse.

good: They went quiet in the way that means it landed.
"Okay." They took their plate to their room.
You apologised twelve minutes later. It half worked.
They looked at you like you were a stranger at a bus stop.
bad: They repeated it to their other parent, word for word.
"You sound like a boss. I'm not one of them."
It went in the ledger. Kids keep a ledger.
They cried and were furious about crying.

good: "Alright, alright. Rough week?" They let you off.
"That's the second one this month, mind."
They laughed it off. The laugh was a bit late.
"You get one of those a year. That was this year's."
bad: "I've known you twenty years and you said that out loud."
They left the group chat. They came back. Still.
"Do you actually like me, or am I just staff now?"
No reply for nine days. That's the reply.

good: "Understood." They shipped it anyway, colder.
The desk around them went very quiet and stayed that way.
They took it on the chin in public and had a word later.
"Right." One word, and a productive, miserable afternoon.
bad: Two people put their headphones on. Everyone heard it.
"That's the sort of thing that ends up in a tribunal, boss."
They updated their profile that evening. Open to work.
"I've been shouted at before. Not by someone I respected."

good: "Bold. I'll give you bold." They did not call back.
They smiled thinly and moved to another conversation.
"Noted." It was, in fact, noted.
The rapport went out of the room like air from a tyre.
bad: It was repeated at three dinners inside a fortnight.
"This industry is small and I'm in most of it."
Their fund passed. The note said 'founder risk'.
They put it in writing so it could be forwarded. It was.

good: Your line made their all-hands. They are properly annoyed.
They subtweeted it, badly, which made it worse for them.
Somebody printed it and pinned it to their wall as motivation.
"We'll remember that at the next raise." They will.
bad: It read as punching up. It made them look like the underdog.
They replied with one word and got twice your reach.
Your own team winced. That's the metric that matters.
They said nothing at all, which cost them nothing at all.

interactions.title: Prank them
interactions.note: Funny is a coin flip and you are holding the coin.

good: Shrieking. Genuine shrieking. Then an immediate revenge plan.
"That was SO good. I hate you. That was so good."
They told the story at dinner for a month.
You got got back within the week. Fair play to them.
bad: You went one step too far and had to sit on the stairs.
"That's not funny, that's just mean." They were right.
Tears, and then a long conversation about trust.
They stopped believing anything you say for a fortnight.

good: "I cannot believe you kept that going for four days."
They fell for it completely and are furious with themselves.
It's already a story they tell about themselves.
"Right. War. You've started a war and you'll lose it."
bad: They'd had a bad week you didn't know about.
It cost them money. Small money, but money.
"Bit old for this, aren't we?"
They laughed and then didn't message for a while.

good: The whole floor was in on it. Best morning in months.
They took it beautifully and started planning the return leg.
Somebody made a poster. The poster is still up.
"Okay, that was good. That was annoyingly good."
bad: It broke a build. The build was for a demo.
Nobody laughs when the boss is the one doing it. Nobody.
"Is this a thing I'm allowed to not find funny?"
HR would like a word, and you don't have an HR.

good: Two hundred pizzas to their office. Petty. Effective.
Their launch stream opened with your logo. Somehow.
They spent a whole morning on it. That's the win.
The industry group chat has not stopped.
bad: It cost them a customer. Now it's not funny, it's a letter.
Their lawyer wrote to your lawyer, who is also you.
It made them sympathetic. Nobody was on your side.
They escalated. They are much better at escalating.

interactions.title: Pick a fight about it
interactions.note: Sometimes the row is the honest thing. Sometimes it is just a row.

good: Forty minutes, loud, and then something actually got decided.
"Finally. I'd rather this than another polite month."
You both said the real thing. The real thing was survivable.
"We're allowed to argue. We're not allowed to go quiet."
bad: It became about 2019. It's always about 2019.
You won it. You could tell you'd won it. That was the problem.
They slept at their sister's. It's happened before.
Nothing was resolved and everything was said.

good: They held their ground. You were quietly impressed.
"Fine. FINE." Then, later, a reasonable compromise.
You both apologised. They went first, which stung.
It cleared the air. Adolescence has weather.
bad: You used your boss voice on a fourteen-year-old.
"You're never here and you're arguing about the rules?"
Door. Music. Two days of one-word answers.
They stopped telling you things. That took months to undo.

good: A proper row, then a pint. That's the format.
"You're wrong, but you're allowed to be wrong at me."
They gave as good as they got and you both felt better.
"Twenty years. We've had worse. Sit down."
bad: You brought up the loan. You should not have brought up the loan.
"I'm not one of your reports."
Silence, then a very short message about Sunday being off.
Other people had to pick a side. They shouldn't have had to.

good: A real disagreement, in the open, and then a decision.
"Good. I'd rather that than another vague standup."
They pushed back hard and were mostly right.
The team saw the boss lose an argument. That's healthy.
bad: You had it in the open plan. Everybody stopped typing.
"I'm not doing this in front of the juniors."
They were right, you were loud, and everyone knew both.
The word 'toxic' got used at lunch. Not to your face.

interactions.title: Give them the silent treatment
interactions.note: Cheap, quiet, and it always costs the same thing in the end.

good: Three days of extremely polite logistics.
They cracked first. You did not enjoy winning.
"Are we doing this? We're doing this."
The house got very tidy. That's how you can tell.
bad: "I can wait longer than you. I've had practice."
They stopped trying to start conversations. That's the bad version.
A week. Then a very calm question about whether this is it.
They told a friend. The friend told you at a party.

good: They noticed on day two and asked what was wrong.
A cold weekend. Then a truce over a takeaway.
"Are you angry at me or at work?" Good question.
You broke first, which was the right way round.
bad: They assumed it was their fault. It was not their fault.
They matched you. Kids are much better at this than adults.
It went in the ledger under a heading you'd rather not read.
Two weeks. They stopped coming downstairs.

good: You went quiet. They noticed, and rang.
"You've gone weird on me. Out with it."
A fortnight of nothing, then a normal Tuesday.
They left one voice note and waited. It worked.
bad: Silence is the default with old friends. Months went by.
"I assumed you were busy." You let them assume it.
They stopped inviting you to things. Not pointedly. Just stopped.
The friendship went into the drawer where friendships go.

good: You stopped stopping at their desk. They noticed by Wednesday.
Their tickets got reassigned without a conversation.
"Have I done something?" Yes. You didn't say what.
They started being early. Anxiety is a productivity tool, briefly.
bad: Managing by silence. The team's word for it, not yours.
"If I'm out, tell me I'm out."
They took the recruiter's call this time.
Two other people started polishing their CVs on principle.

interactions.title: Throw them under the bus
interactions.note: Somebody has to carry it into the room. It doesn't have to be you.

good: The board bought it. Your name stayed clean. Theirs didn't.
"That's not what happened and you know it." Said quietly, after.
It worked. They watched it work from the other side of the table.
Nobody corrected you. Several people could have.
bad: Someone had the thread. The thread said otherwise.
"I've got the email, boss." They had the email.
The room believed them, not you. Slowly, then completely.
They resigned in the meeting. Then they told the meeting why.

good: The blame landed elsewhere. They noticed where.
"Interesting version of events." No comment beyond that.
It held. It held at a price you'll pay later.
They stopped answering, which is cheaper than a lawsuit.
bad: They were in the room. You did not know they were in the room.
It reached their fund's partners before it reached yours.
"You used my name to cover a mess I warned you about."
Two intros evaporated by Friday.

interactions.title: Threaten them
interactions.note: Legal calls this 'a conversation about consequences'.

good: They stayed. They stayed the way people stay in a hostage video.
"Fine. I'll do it." And they did it, and hated it.
The notice period got mentioned. Loudly. It worked.
They folded quickly, which told you something about their year.
bad: "Put that in writing." You did not put it in writing.
They recorded it. Phones are very good now.
They quit on the spot and told the group chat why.
The word 'constructive dismissal' entered your life.

good: They backed off. Quietly, and permanently.
"Alright. No need for that." There had been need for that.
It stopped the thing you wanted stopped.
They stopped copying you into anything, which was the point.
bad: They forwarded it to four people with 'FYI'.
"You've just made this much more interesting for me."
Their lawyer replied. Their lawyer is a real lawyer.
It became a story about you at three different dinners.

good: They took it seriously enough to change a launch date.
Their comms team asked for a call. That's a win, of sorts.
You are now genuinely a problem they think about on Sundays.
"Understood." Cold, brief, and rattled.
bad: They published it. In full. With a headline.
It got them a funding round's worth of sympathy.
Their lawyer is better than yours and everybody now knows.
You handed them the villain slot and took it yourself.

interactions.title: Ask them for money
interactions.note: The money only arrives if they say yes. The asking costs either way.

good: "How much do you need?" Asked without a flicker. Terrifying.
They transferred it and made one joke about interest.
"You paid for eighteen years of me. Take it."
"Don't tell mum." Deal.
bad: "You're asking me?" They will remember that you asked.
They said yes and it changed something between you.
"I haven't got it. I'm sorry. I really haven't got it."
It went in the ledger. Right at the top of the ledger.

good: "Sent. Pay me back when you can, or don't."
"Course. Don't make it weird and don't make it a habit."
No questions. That's what twenty years buys.
"On one condition: you take a Saturday off."
bad: "I can't, mate. I want to, and I can't."
They said yes and asked for it in writing. Both hurt.
"Is the company alright? Be honest with me." You weren't.
The conversation got very formal very quickly.

good: "Personal money? Unusual. Fine. Small, and it's a favour."
They wired it and said nothing about it again.
"I've been where you are. Don't make me regret it."
"This isn't an investment. Don't dress it up as one."
bad: "That's not really what I do. Talk to the fund properly."
They said no in the nicest available words.
"You've just told me your balance sheet without meaning to."
Your name got a small asterisk on somebody's list.

interactions.title: Lend them money
interactions.note: Out of your wallet. You may see it again.

good: "I'll pay it back." They wrote it down themselves.
It got them out of something they hadn't told you about.
"Thanks. Properly, thanks."
They paid back half within a month. Unprompted.
bad: It's the fourth time and everyone knows it's the fourth time.
"So it's fine when it's money." Ouch.
You attached a lecture. The lecture was the expensive part.
They took it and stopped mentioning the thing it was for.

good: "You've saved me. I'm not being dramatic. You've saved me."
They insisted on a date and hit the date.
"Right. Now nobody mentions this ever again."
They named it a loan out loud so it stayed a loan.
bad: Nobody set terms. Nobody ever sets terms.
"I didn't ask for this." They hadn't.
It sat between you at every dinner after that.
They went quiet for two months out of embarrassment.

good: A quiet advance, no paperwork. They never mentioned it again.
"I won't forget this." They didn't.
It solved the thing that had been eating their sprints.
"That stays between us, yeah?" It did.
bad: Somebody found out. Now two other people have a question.
"Is this a loan or a leash?" Reasonable question.
It made the salary conversation impossible for a year.
Payroll noticed. Payroll is one spreadsheet and one person.

good: "Bridge accepted. You've bought yourself a friend."
They paid it back with a warm intro attached.
"Not many people would have. I'll remember."
It cleared their problem and opened their book.
bad: "That's very kind and slightly odd."
They took it and the relationship became a ledger.
It looked like buying access. It was buying access.
Their compliance officer wrote a paragraph about it.

interactions.title: Ask them for a favour
interactions.note: Favours are a currency and this spends some.

good: "Done. Don't even think about it."
They made a call you couldn't have made. It worked.
"You never ask. So obviously, yes."
Sorted by Thursday, with a photo as proof.
bad: "That's the third one this year, you know."
They did it, and it clearly cost them something.
"I'd rather you asked me to the pub sometimes instead."
"Can't do that one, sorry." Said carefully.

good: "Yeah, I'll sort it." And they sorted it, off the books.
They stayed late without being asked to stay late.
"You could have just put it in the sprint, but fine."
Done, quietly, before anybody noticed it needed doing.
bad: "Is this a favour or is this my job now?"
It ate their evening. They had plans. They had told you.
They did it and logged the hours somewhere you'd see.
"I'm going to say no this time." Good for them.

good: "Sure. You're due one." You were not due one.
The intro came through the same afternoon.
"Happy to. Remember this next time I ask."
One email from them opened a door two months of yours hadn't.
bad: "I don't really know them well enough to do that."
"That's a big ask from someone I've met twice."
They forwarded it and did not vouch for you.
"Let's build the relationship a bit first." Meaning no.

interactions.title: End it
interactions.note: The home stays. The kids stay. Nothing else does.

good: It was calm, which was the worst available version.
"I've been waiting for you to say it for about a year."
They packed on a Sunday. You helped carry things to the car.
bad: "You're doing this on a Tuesday. Over the company."
They asked one question and you didn't have an answer.
The kids heard the whole thing through the floor.

interactions.title: Start something with them
interactions.note: A fact, and a secret with a shelf life.

good: Nobody at either company knows. For now, nobody at either company knows.
Two phones. One of them is new. That's how these start.
"We're being very stupid." Agreed, and not stopping.
bad: A waiter recognised you. Small city, small industry.
You were photographed at a launch you'd both said you'd skip.
Somebody's assistant put two calendars side by side.

interactions.title: Disown them
interactions.note: They stay your kid. Nothing else about it survives.

good: They took it better than you did, which was the last insult.
"Right," they said. "Right." And that was the conversation.
They asked you to say it once more so they'd believe it.
bad: They laughed, because they thought you were joking.
Your other kids found out within the hour.
They left the family group chat. The name stayed in it.

interactions.title: Fire them, with cause
interactions.note: Named, on the record, and they do not come back through the book.

good: Box, badge, lift. Twenty minutes, and legal says it's clean.
You said the reason out loud. Nobody argued with the reason.
The floor was quiet and slightly relieved. That happens.
bad: They said their version on the way out and it sounded better.
Two people followed them out within the month.
Your reason will be in somebody's reference call for years.

interactions.title: Taunt them in public
interactions.note: Grudge up either way. The roll decides who looks better.

good: Your line got picked up. Theirs did not.
The quote made two newsletters and one of their standups.
"Competition is healthy," they said, visibly unhealthy.
Your team put it on a mug. An actual mug.
bad: It read as obsessed, because it was slightly obsessed.
They ignored it and looked enormous doing so.
The replies were about you, and not kindly.
One of your own investors asked you to stop.

interactions.title: Sabotage their launch
interactions.note: Deniable. Mostly deniable.

good: Their launch day went sideways and nobody knows why.
The reviewer got the wrong build. Somehow. Terrible luck.
Their announcement landed in the middle of somebody else's news.
Two of their integrations broke in the same hour. Extraordinary.
bad: It was traced to somebody who has your company on their CV.
It made their week's numbers *better*. Sympathy sells.
Somebody kept the messages. Somebody always keeps the messages.
Your own team worked it out. That's a morale problem now.

interactions.title: Offer to bury it
interactions.note: The grudge comes down. It doesn't come down to nothing.

good: A drink, no press, no lawyers. It genuinely helped.
"We're both going to lose to the same giant anyway." True.
You agreed on one thing publicly and it cost you both nothing.
"Truce." Said properly, with a handshake and a bad joke.
bad: They took the meeting and briefed against you afterwards.
"Very generous of the smaller company." That word again.
It was read as weakness by everybody, including your board.
They agreed and changed nothing at all.
